gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's built-in solar ports are capped at 12–60 V and 20 A each, so BLUETTI's own 500 W panel (49.1 V Voc, 12.22 A Imp) fits only one per port: that is 1,000 W of panel, not the 2,400 W headline, unless you add a SolarX 4K. They also don't state that the unit's measured 19.5 W inverter idle draw uses about 468 Wh a day before any load runs.
standout_why: EnergySage (cited) lists the Apex 300 at '2,400 W (more with SolarX 4K)' max solar input. It gives no voltage or current limit per port, says only that panels must stay 'within the unit's voltage and wattage limits', and does not mention idle draw. Solar Waypoint (cited) gives per-port voltage windows only for the F3800 Plus (11–165 V, 17 A) and the DELTA Pro Ultra, and says nothing about idle or self-consumption for either. thisWATT (cited) would not load (TLS certificate error), so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer showed 'Apex 300 … 2,400 W solar input' and a sizing table with no inverter overhead. No rival page I read turns the port limit into a panel count, or the idle draw into a daily energy cost. Both decide how many panels go in the cart and whether the SolarX 4K is needed.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh LFP, 3,840 W, 120/240 V). It is already in the Dealectric catalog. ESS News measured its idle draw with the inverters on at 19.5 W, about half of what owners report for the F3800 Plus (unsourced, see below), and that matters when the unit runs 24/7 off grid.
Expansion batteries: 2× BLUETTI B300K (2,764.8 Wh each), for 8,294.4 Wh total. The idle draw uses 468 Wh a day (19.5 W × 24 h), about 5.6% of 8,294.4 Wh, compared with 16.9% of a lone Apex 300.

Solar panels: 2× BLUETTI SORA 500 (500 W), one per built-in port. Two panels in series would reach 98.2 V Voc, above the 60 V limit. Two in parallel would draw 24.44 A at max power, above the 20 A limit, so a third or fourth panel adds nothing without a SolarX 4K.
Optional, for more than about 1 kW of panels: BLUETTI SolarX 4K (500 V Voc, 4,000 W according to BLUETTI's bundle listing). It takes high-voltage series strings, which the 60 V built-in ports cannot.
Optional: BLUETTI Solar Extension Cable (MC4, 30 A, 5 m or 10 m), so the panels can sit in full sun away from the unit.

Higher-solar option without panels: Apex 300 + 2*B300K + SolarX 4K at $4,498.00 (https://www.bluettipower.com/products/apex-300-2-b300k-solarx-4k).

findings.label: Measured idle self-consumption, inverters on
findings.source_title: Hands-on with the Bluetti Apex 300 portable power station (Tristan Rayner, ESS News, 2025-09-17)
findings.note: Unit idle with the inverters on, 'around 19.5 W per hour while we watched'. The article does not say whether it was in 120 V or 240 V mode. Arithmetic: 19.5 W × 24 h = 468 Wh/day. 468 / 2,764.8 Wh = 16.9% of a lone Apex 300 each day. 468 / 8,294.4 Wh = 5.6% with 2× B300K.

findings.label: Measured idle draw (second source) and AC efficiency
findings.source_title: Bluetti Apex 300 review (The Solar Lab, no author or date shown)
findings.note: A single unit in standby. The Solar Lab says a full unit would drain in about 6 days; check: 2,764.8 Wh / (20 W × 24 h) = 5.8 days. At 85%, 2,764.8 Wh gives about 2,350 Wh delivered.

findings.label: Maker's stated idle loss
findings.note: The product page says the unit 'cut idle loss to just 20W'. This matches the ESS News measurement.

findings.label: Built-in solar input limits
findings.note: From the spec table. 60 V × 20 A = 1,200 W, so a port reaches its rating only with a string near 60 V at 20 A. BLUETTI's US page had an empty Tech Specs section.

findings.label: Panel electrical specs
findings.value: Voc 49.1 V, Vmp 40.92 V, Imp 12.22 A, Isc 13.31 A
findings.source_title: The Bluetti Sora 500 Solar Panel Review (Andrew Paul, Impulse Gamer, 2026-08-02)
findings.note: Spec table from the review; BLUETTI's US page lists no Voc/Imp. Port fit: 2 in series = 98.2 V Voc, above the 60 V limit, so not allowed. 2 in parallel = 24.44 A Imp, above the 20 A limit, so output is clipped to about 20 A × 40.92 V = 818 W. That means one panel per port, 2 × 500 W = 1,000 W on the built-in ports. Even the parallel case tops out at about 1,637 W across both ports, never 2,400 W.

findings.label: Measured real-world output
findings.source_title: The Bluetti Sora 500 Solar Panel Review (Andrew Paul, Impulse Gamer, 2026-08-02)
findings.note: Measured in Australian winter, connected to a Bluetti Elite 300. Arithmetic: 2 panels × 400 W = 800 W. Covering the 468 Wh/day idle takes about 0.6 h of that output (468 / 800). Refilling one 2,764.8 Wh pack takes about 3.5 h of that output (2,764.8 / 800), before charge losses.
